title: Skill pipelines: contextual onboarding deck for empty states
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Create a reusable, persona-aware onboarding "skill pipeline" — a short deck of contextual micro-lessons and interactive tasks that appear in empty states across the Redwood Console (Projects, Models, Rollouts, Cost Explorer). The pipeline should introduce 2–4 concrete actions tailored to the user's persona (developer, platform engineer, product manager) and workspace activity level.

Scope: Design a lightweight deck component, a compact ribbon trigger, and 2 templated pipelines for initial rollout: 
1) QuickStart Developer pipeline for generating a first model request and inspecting traces.
2) Platform Onboard pipeline for Dedicated/Private teams to configure routing and capacity.

Out of scope for this ticket: backend personalization algorithm, metrics collection plumbing, and localized copy (will be separate). This ticket focuses on UX patterns, visual language, templates, and a prototype for user testing.

Constraints & considerations: Should fit into existing empty-state containers without pushing primary CTAs. Must be dismissible, resumable (persisted per workspace), and minimal (3 steps recommended). Must work in narrow side panels and full-width empty canvases. Avoid overlapping with existing coach overlays and ensure compatibility with rollouts and cost hint cards.
acceptance_criteria: A responsive deck component (figma prototype) that demonstrates 3-step developer and 3-step platform pipelines in both narrow and full-width empty states.
Copy and interaction specs for: trigger ribbon, card progression, success state, skip/dismiss, resume from last step.
Design tokens and spacing rules consistent with Console design system; accessible contrast and keyboard focus states defined.
Annotated handoff file with states and transitions, and a lightweight interaction spec for engineering (keyboard, screen-reader hints, events to persist progress).
Usability test plan and results (5 unmoderated participants) with identified changes and sign-off from PM.

review_feedback: PM — Priya: Add an optional "Try with sample data" CTA on the first card for Developer pipeline (users responded positively in study).
Eng — Marco: Recommend emitting lifecycle events: opened, completed_step_{n}, dismissed. Avoid heavy client-side state; provide server persistence option.
Accessibility — Noor: Ensure focus trap for modal-like decks; non-modal ribbon must not disrupt screen reader flow. Provide aria-live updates for step completion.
decision_log: 2026-02-03 — Decided to cap pipeline length at 3 steps to reduce cognitive load.
2026-02-05 — Decided to implement both client-resume (localStorage) and optional server persist (API) to support multi-device resumption.
2026-02-10 — Decided to surface a small progress chip on empty state when pipeline is partially completed, instead of auto-launching on return.
